title: Ziggurat of Aqar Quf (Dur-Kurigalzu)
summary: The ziggurat at Aqar Quf, in the ancient Kassite city of Dur-Kurigalzu near Baghdad, was built by King Kurigalzu; the city dates to around 1400 BCE. The mudbrick tower is roughly square, about 69 by 67.6 m at the base, and still stands tens of metres high. Iraq's Directorate of Antiquities excavated it in 1942 to 1946.

uncertainty.note: Founding date of the city, c. 1400 B.C., from the Historical Dictionary of Mesopotamia; Penn Museum names the builder but gives no date.

where.modern_name: Aqar Quf ziggurat, Abu Ghraib, Baghdad Governorate, Iraq

importance.justification: One of the best-preserved ziggurats of Mesopotamia, in the Kassite royal city, on Iraq's UNESCO Tentative List since January 2025.

measurements.note: still stands to a height of 57 meters today; Penn Museum (1948) says it towers more than two hundred feet above the plain, so the surviving height is not settled

phases.description: Built by the Kassite king Kurigalzu at the founding of Dur-Kurigalzu, around 1400 B.C.; the tower still stands.

model.no_mesh: Two sources disagree on the surviving height (57 m in the Historical Dictionary of Mesopotamia; more than two hundred feet in a 1948 Penn Museum bulletin), and neither is a measured survey, so the figures stay as data and no mesh is drawn.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the height: 57 m (Historical Dictionary, hosted on en-academic.com) vs more than 200 feet (Penn 1948); no measured institutional survey found, hence no_mesh. Shape ziggurat is the closest form. The date is the city foundation, not a dated ziggurat build.
